Evan —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our MAP (attached v3), the immediate open item before contract finalization is alignment on the performance budget: latency SLOs (P95), TTFT for common prompt lengths, throughput at target concurrency, and the acceptable degradation modes.

Quick summary of what we need from Peregrine this week so our engineering team can finalize the Dedicated capacity sizing and the SLA in the contract:
- Your canonical test harness and raw results (CSV preferred).
- The exact request shapes (prompt lengths, system instructions, streaming on/off).
- Whether your tests were cold-cache or warm-cache and any KV-cache priming steps.

We ran a set of internal microbenchmarks this morning (attached runbook and load script) against the trial model and saw: P95 latency ~ 180ms (token-streaming off), TTFT ~ 420ms for 128-token prompts, steady throughput ~ 1,200 tokens/s at 64 concurrent sessions (continuous batching enabled). We expect some delta vs your numbers because we default to continuous batching + prefix caching.

Please attach your results and a sample command that reproduces your run so Rishi and Connor can triage methodology differences. I propose a 30-min method alignment call Thursday 6/3 — are you available?

Our runs were cold-cache (no priming) to reflect first-touch user experience. Key numbers: P95 latency 350–420ms, TTFT ~ 900ms on average for 128-token prompts, throughput roughly 700 tokens/s at 100 concurrent VUs.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick triage of Peregrine numbers before alignment call

Team —

I parsed Peregrine's CSV and ran a couple of controlled reproductions in our QA infra to validate the delta. Short version: their P95/TTFT are ~2x ours; plausible causes we should bring up on the call:
1) Cold vs warm cache: cold-cache adds KV cache population on first requests — can add ~200–400ms depending on prefix reuse.
2) Batching: their harness was single-request-per-VU (no continuous batching). Our runtime defaults to multi-request batching at the transport layer; batching reduces per-token overhead by ~30–50% in our tests.
3) Concurrency semantics: k6 VUs != concurrent sessions in our gateway. k6 tends to serialize some connection reuse; we need to compare connection pools, keep-alive settings, and WebSocket vs HTTP streaming.
4) Quantization / model variant: confirm Peregrine was hitting the same model (we used rwd-gpt-medium-quant-v2). Customer might have used a smaller/larger variant or older checkpoint.

I attach a short repro script (rwd-repro-runbook.sh) that sets up identical conditions: priming pass, identical request pacing, and a k6-compatible script. If they truly need cold-cache numbers, we can add a cold-run block to the MAP and document the expected delta in the contract.

Action items for call:
- Confirm exact model binary and quantization used by Peregrine (Connor)
- Walk through k6 script differences (Connor)
- Agree canonical test sequence (cold-run then warm steady-state), sample sizes, and success criteria (TL;DR: P95 <= 250ms for warm steady-state, TTFT <= 500ms at target concurrency)

Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Rishi/Aisha —

Thanks, Rishi. We attempted to reproduce with the runbook but hit two issues:
- Our k6 harness shows connection churn that appears to increase latency; we set keep-alive but saw intermittent 502s at scale. We're attaching a snippet of our k6 config.
- Model variant: Peregrine's test used open-gpt-large v1 (we requested the model from your catalog, but the trial token we used selected a different binary). That alone could explain a 30–40% difference.

We're happy to run the canonical sequence (cold then warm) but need a bit more guidance: do you have a minimal k6 scenario we can drop in that mirrors your batching/keep-alive and will not cause the 502 churn? Also, will Redwood provide a pinned model binary or recommendation for the exact image to use in the Dedicated preview?

If we can get that by EOD 6/6, we can run the suite and get you results before your contract signoff next week.

Evan

Evan —

Sorry about the churn you saw. I've put together a minimal k6 script and a small gateway config that mirrors our connection pool + keep-alive settings; attaching rwd-loadscript-k6.js and the repro runbook (rwd-repro-runbook.sh). The key differences we enforce in the script:
- persistent HTTP/1.1 connections with explicit keep-alive headers
- request pacing that allows the client's per-connection pipeline to stay saturated (avoids k6 VU sleep jitter)
- an initial priming pass of 50 unique prompts to warm KV prefixes

If you run the attached script against the pinned model endpoint (we can send that as an IP+token for the Dedicated preview), you should see warm P95 numbers closer to the ones we reported. If you prefer, I can stand up an isolated test endpoint with pre-warmed cache for you to run the suite.

Propose we do a 30-min runbook + live repro call on 6/9 10:00 PT to walk through the script and watch a run. Connor will drive the repro steps; Rishi will monitor server-side metrics; Aisha/Marissa will attend for MAP decisioning.

Date: 2026-06-10T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: MAP update — reconciliation outcomes, MAP timeline adjustments, and contract milestone sync

Evan/Layla/Procurement —

Thanks for running the tests and for the live repro session. Short summary and MAP updates (see MAP v3 for full timeline):
- Outcome: once standardized on the pinned model image and after a priming pass, warm steady-state convergence reduced P95 by ~40% in Peregrine's runs. Final validated warm P95: 220–260ms; TTFT: 460–520ms at 64 logical concurrent sessions (we matched session semantics to your traffic shape).
- Remaining delta: ~60–80ms in tail latency driven by network serialization at Peregrine's edge (their load generator environment introduced head-of-line queuing under certain TCP reuse patterns). We documented mitigations in the MAP (connection pool tuning and short keep-alive timeouts).
- Contract impact: based on the validated warm steady-state numbers, Redwood will commit to the Dedicated SLO of P95 <= 300ms and TTFT <= 600ms for the first 12 months; see clause 4.2 in the MAP. Cold-cache single-request experience will be documented as an informational metric and excluded from SLA.

Next steps and owners (dates are in MAP):
- 6/12: Connor to provide pinned endpoint + test token for Peregrine (Connor)
- 6/13: Peregrine to run full suite (cold then warm) and upload raw CSV to shared Drive (Evan)
- 6/16: Redwood to produce formal benchmarking appendix with methodology and signed reproducibility checklist (Rishi/Marissa)
- 6/18: Legal to fold SLO language into final Dedicated contract and route for signature (Aisha / procurement@peregrine.com)

If procurement needs any change to the dates, flag it in the thread and we'll accommodate. Thanks all — this is a good outcome for both teams.

Best,
Aisha Rahman

Redwood Inference
